prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through PROTACs and the molecular basis of glue degraders.

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a chemical idea that changed what a small molecule is expected to do: instead of occupying an active site, a designed molecule brings a ligase and a target together and the cell does the rest, catalytically and with access to targets that lack pockets. It is the only shortlisted candidate that seven of eight members placed in their top three, and it has been reproduced by many independent groups, with structural and biophysical work on ternary complexes (cooperativity, linker design) giving it real chemical depth. My opening ballot named Ciulli as the third laureate. The colleagues' arguments make me reconsider: five of the seven other members proposed Handa, and the cereblon discovery is what turns thalidomide-type drugs from a clinical accident into a mechanistically understood class. A prize that covers both the heterobifunctional concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the glue mechanism (Handa) is more coherent than one that covers only the PROTAC strand.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved yet, so the prize would rest on conceptual and mechanistic foundations and early clinical signals rather than a delivered medicine. The three-person limit also forces an unfair omission: Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work, Gray's chemical-probe contributions, Sakamoto and Kim as the first authors of the 2001 PROTAC paper, and Ito all go unrecognised. The PROTAC and glue lineages are historically distinct, and a joint citation may blur two achievements that a committee could prefer to treat separately.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics should be first: it is a clean two-person attribution, very mature, and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution is the cleanest on the list and that maturity is not in doubt. My reservation is about breadth of consequence rather than quality: I give more weight to a discovery that opened a new class of therapeutics and many new experiments on previously undruggable targets than to a method whose impact, though large, is mostly enabling for other work. I would keep B061 as a strong alternative but not ahead of B020. I note that you also ranked B020 second, so our disagreement concerns order, not merit.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling should be first because of three decades of industrial use, with PROTACs seen as somewhat premature given no approvals.
responses.response: The prematurity concern is fair, and I do not dismiss it. But Buchwald-Hartwig chemistry extends the cross-coupling theme recognised in 2010, and the committee would have to argue why C-N bond formation is a distinct achievement. Degraders have been confirmed mechanistically by independent groups, by structures of ternary complexes, and by many clinical-stage compounds. I would accept waiting for the first approval if the committee judged clinical proof essential, but I do not think the Chemistry prize has treated approval as a requirement when the chemical principle is established.

responses.point: Nitrogenase should be first, because the atomic structures of the FeMo-cofactor give a concrete mechanism for a hard redox transformation, and the structural picture has been stable for decades.
responses.response: The structural case is strong and I respect the maturity argument. However, the substrate-binding mechanism is by your own assessment still partly open, and only one member placed nitrogenase in the top eight, so it is not a candidate with committee-wide traction. I also share your view that B020 attribution cannot cover everyone, and I have moved toward your Handa choice. I would not stand in the way of nitrogenase later if the committee prefers a fundamental-mechanism prize.

responses.point: Degraders reframe pharmacology as event-driven catalysis rather than occupancy, and Handa's cereblon work explains the glue mechanism. The lack of an approved PROTAC drug is a modest timing concern.
responses.response: I agree with the framing and have adopted the Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio in place of my opening choice of Ciulli. I would press one point: Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands are what turned the concept into rational design, so omitting him is a real cost, and the citation should be worded to credit the field broadly rather than imply the three are the only contributors.

responses.point: Biomolecular phase separation recasts cell organisation as a physical-chemical problem, and ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a self-assembly solution to nucleic-acid delivery. Both are put ahead of the degraders.
responses.response: As someone who works on peptide self-assembly I find both compelling, and the overlap in our fields does not make them equally ready. Condensate biology is still contested about which cellular structures are truly phase separated, so I would be cautious about a citation that has to commit to a physiological interpretation. The lipid nanoparticle case is stronger, but the Medicine 2023 mRNA prize and the disputed credit among Cullis, Anderson, Langer and the Vancouver group make it harder to assign than degraders. I keep B010 as an alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize without an approved PROTAC drug, or wait for first approvals.
Whether Handa, rather than Ciulli, Gray or Sakamoto and Kim, is the right third name, and whether one citation can fairly span the PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages.
My priority details come from general knowledge and have not been independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. None of the shortlisted laureate candidates is a known collaborator or mentor of mine; I have only a field-level interest in peptide and nanoparticle self-assembly (relevant to B010 and B024), which does not require recusal.
